- **Keep the public mdBook (`docs/book/`) current — update it in the same PR as any user-facing change.** Before opening a PR, check whether the work changes public API, the quickstart/example flow, the crate roster (incl. a stub crate ascending to published), or a documented concept; if so, bring the affected `docs/book/src/*.md` page(s) into line on the same branch. The book is published from `main` and drifts silently otherwise — it sat as the untouched SMA-311 scaffold (13/17 pages still `> **Stub.**`) through all of Stage 1 before anyone noticed; SMA-423 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no book edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip. `mdbook build docs/book` must stay clean (`[output.linkcheck] warning-policy = "error"`).
- **Keep crate `README.md` files current — update the affected crate's README in the same PR as any change to its public surface.** Each of the ten published crates' `README.md` is its crates.io (and docs.rs landing-sidebar) page — no crate sets an explicit `readme`, so Cargo uses the default `README.md`. Before opening a PR, for every crate the work touches check whether the change affects that crate's public API / usage example, its install or feature story, or its published status (a stub ascending to published, a renamed/added feature flag); if so, bring its `crates/<crate>/README.md` into line on the same branch — and also the facade `crates/paigasus-helikon/README.md` and the root `README.md` whenever the crate roster or the feature → module map changes. README install snippets deliberately use drift-free `cargo add` (no hardcoded versions), so a routine version bump alone needs no README edit. Like the mdBook, the READMEs drift silently otherwise — they sat as untouched 3-line SMA-304 stubs (`Stub — see SMA-304`) through all of Stage 1 while ten crates shipped real implementations; SMA-424 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no README edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip.
- Commit prefix: `<type>(<scope>): SMA-### <message>` (e.g. `feat(facade): SMA-304 ...`).
- **PR titles must satisfy two independent rules from `pr-title.yml`** (`amannn/action-semantic-pull-request`):
  1. **Full Conventional Commits format.** The action enforces a valid `type(scope):` prefix from the action's configured `types` list — independent of the subject regex. `SMA-317 add anthropic provider` (no prefix) fails; `feat(providers-anthropic): SMA-317 add anthropic provider` passes.
  2. **Subject must start lowercase after the `SMA-###` prefix.** The `subjectPattern: ^([A-Z]{2,4}-\d+ )?[^A-Z].+$` rejects `feat(core): SMA-314 LlmAgent + ...` because `L` is uppercase; lead the subject with a lowercase verb (`add`, `wire`, `pin`, `promote`, `implement`, `fix`).
  Per-commit Conventional Commit titles on the feature branch don't trip either rule — only the PR title (which becomes the squashed `main` commit) is gated.
- Linear auto-closes the linked SMA-* issue when its PR merges; no manual status move needed.
- **Always implement GitHub Actions against the latest stable major**, pinned to a commit SHA (never a moving `@vN` tag), keeping the human-readable version as a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment **on the `uses:` line**, so the SHA is auditable. The comment must end with the version: Dependabot updates only a same-line comment that ends with the old version, so a version on its own line above the step goes stale on every bump (SMA-744). This rule applies only to pins of a tagged release. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is pinned to an untagged `master` commit, so it has no version comment. Do not add one, because no tag gives a correct version. The `gh-actions` Dependabot group sets no `update-types`, so its configuration permits major bumps in the same grouped PR. Do not depend on that: `actions/checkout` still sat on v6.0.2 until SMA-486 bumped it by hand, so **check for a new major by hand**. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is a special case: it ships rolling branches and a periodically re-pointed `v1` tag, so confirm the direction (`ahead_by > 0, behind_by == 0`) before accepting any bump — the naive "bump to latest release" recipe once would have proposed an ~11-month downgrade. Independently and permanently: every site pinning it **must** pair the SHA with an explicit `with: toolchain: …`, because a SHA ref carries no toolchain selector. Recipes and history: `docs/runbooks/github-actions-pinning.md`.
- **After a PR merges to `main`, release-plz opens/updates a `chore: release` PR** (authored by the paigasusbot App) carrying the version bumps + CHANGELOG; in the normal flow **merging that PR is what publishes to crates.io** (the merged feature PR left versions matching the registry, so its own `main` push publishes nothing). The exception is a PR that bumps its own version — the stub-ascend ritual — which publishes on its own merge with no separate release PR. Check the release PR after every merge and watch its CI — its release-PR `cargo update` can pull a fresh advisory that reddens `audit`/`deny` on the bot PR **only** (independent of `main`); fix with a `chore(deps)` pin and release-plz regenerates the PR clean.

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs nine jobs on every PR (`commits` is PR-only; the other eight also run on push to `main`): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test` (matrix `{ubuntu, macos, windows} × {stable, 1.94}`, `fail-fast: false`), `build-no-default-features`, `docs` (`RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`), `doc-coverage` (gated at `DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD`, default 80%), `commits` (`convco check`), `sessions-it` (Postgres/Redis, path-filtered), and `markdown-lint`. The `paigasus-helikon-cli` crate is excluded from both the `missing_docs` lint and the coverage aggregator until its public API stabilizes.

`.github/workflows/integration.yml` runs `temporal-it` and `agentcore-image` as **signal-only** jobs, deliberately outside `ci.yml` so an expected flake cannot make "ci is red on `main`" meaningless. **Signal-only means *not listed as required*, never `continue-on-error`.**

`.github/workflows/msrv.yml` runs `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify` as a non-required signal that the declared MSRV is truthful.

Supply-chain workflows (`audit.yml`, `deny.yml`, `sbom.yml`) are separate from `ci.yml` because they have independent triggers and failure semantics. `audit.yml` and `deny.yml` both run on push to `main`, PRs, a daily cron, and `workflow_dispatch`, so `main` is re-evaluated daily at exactly PR severity.

**To read an audit verdict, use the Checks API, not the legacy commit-status API** — the latter returns only `CodeRabbit` on this repo, rendering a confident `state: success` that contains no audit verdict whatsoever:

```bash
gh api repos/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/commits/main/check-runs \
  --jq '.check_runs[] | select(.name=="audit" or .name=="deny") | {name, status, conclusion}'
```

Note also that the `scheduled-audit` job's green status means nothing at any severity — read the *run* conclusion, never that job's status.

The required-status-check contexts gated on `main` are (bare job names, as posted by the GitHub Actions app): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test (ubuntu-latest, stable)`, `test (macos-latest, stable)`, `test (windows-latest, stable)`, `docs`, `doc-coverage`, `book-build`, `commits`, `pr-title`, `audit`, `deny`, `sessions-it`, `build-no-default-features`, `markdown-lint`. The macOS job is required because it is the only gate that compiles and runs the Seatbelt backend; the Windows job because it is the only gate that exercises the Windows timeout path in `paigasus-helikon-tools` — `cmd /C` process spawning and a `TerminateProcess`-based kill, which unlike the unix path has no process-group semantics and assigns a real exit code (SMA-569); `sessions-it` because it is the only gate that runs the live Postgres/Redis session backends; `build-no-default-features` because it is the only gate that compiles `runtime-axum` and `runtime-actix` with default features off. The canonical declaration is `.github/rulesets/main-protection-checks.json` (see CONTRIBUTING.md → "Repo configuration"). Other matrix variants (the `1.94` legs) run as signals only.

These pins are hand-bumped with nothing tracking them: `TEMPORAL_CLI_VERSION`/`TEMPORAL_CLI_SHA256` in `integration.yml`, `NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN` in `ci.yml`, `convco@…` in `ci.yml`'s `commits` job, `MDBOOK_VERSION`/`MDBOOK_LINKCHECK_VERSION` in `docs.yml`, and `markdownlint-cli2` via `package-lock.json`. **A checksum mismatch is never a signal to update the digest** — the causes are, in order, a truncated download, an upstream re-tag, and tampering; verify upstream independently first.

**The workspace needs no system `protoc`** (SMA-623): `temporalio-client`'s `vendored-protox` feature compiles the Temporal protos with `protox`. `ci.yml` sets `PROTOC` to a path that does not exist, and `build-no-default-features` asserts that the feature is active. If a build fails with "Could not find `protoc`", do not add a `protoc` install — find which build script calls it. Rationale and recovery: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "protoc and protox".

Job-by-job rationale, the audit/deny signal semantics, and the incident history behind all of the above: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md`.

**GitHub's 10 GB Actions cache limit is a standing constraint, not a one-time cleanup** (SMA-618): it is GitHub's **default**, not a hard ceiling — a repo admin, org owner or enterprise owner can raise it (user-owned repos up to 10 TB) at additional storage cost, and SMA-618 deliberately chose to fit inside it rather than pay. Enforced at 10 **GiB** (10,737,418,240 bytes) despite the "10 GB" wording. Going over fails nothing — it just triggers silent LRU eviction that makes CI legs run cold at random. `cache-budget.yml` monitors it daily and warns (never fails) above 8.5 GiB. Caches are saved **only** from `main` (`save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}` on every `Swatinem/rust-cache` site) so a PR job can still restore an entry `main` wrote but never writes a competing `refs/pull/N/merge` entry that evicts it. The `CARGO_*`/`RUST*`-prefixed workflow env that `rust-cache` hashes into its key must stay byte-identical across every cache-bearing workflow, enforced by `scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh` running as a step in `fmt`. `audit` and `deny` deliberately cache no `target/` directory — neither compiles the workspace, so it was pure waste against the fixed budget.  CI also sets **`CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only`** (SMA-618 PR 2), which measured a **16.5% cut in total cache bytes** — 14-29% on the `test` legs and exactly 0% on `clippy`/`docs`/`doc-coverage`, which are metadata-mode builds with no debug info to remove. (A local sample of the largest `.rlib` files suggested 79%; do not extrapolate an aggregate from its densest component.) Keeping line tables preserves file:line in panic backtraces. Like `CARGO_TERM_COLOR`, it is **inside** rust-cache's key, so it must be byte-identical in every cache-bearing workflow — adding it to one and not the rest silently splits the cache rather than failing. `prefix-key: v1` marks the post-PR-2 generation, so any surviving `v0-` entry is provably stale and safe to purge — note it **replaces** the default `v0-rust` entirely, so keys read `v1-<job>-...`, not `v1-rust-<job>-...`. `clippy` and `docs` share one entry via `shared-key: metadata`, with `clippy` the sole writer and `docs` carrying a literal `save-if: false`; exactly one site may save a shared key, and the guard enforces it. Full rationale: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "Actions cache budget".

The **`microvm`/forkd live-KVM path is not validated locally or in GitHub CI** — the dev host is arm64 macOS (no `/dev/kvm`) and GitHub runners have none. Validate it on a **GCP nested-virtualization VM** (Ubuntu 24.04 — the forkd binaries need glibc ≥ 2.38; Intel `n2`) per `docs/runbooks/forkd-live-validation.md`. The `tests/forkd_live.rs` tests are env-gated (`FORKD_URL` / `FORKD_TOKEN` / `FORKD_SNAPSHOT`) and loud-skip when no controller is configured, so `cargo test` stays green without one.

## Local hooks

Hooks are managed via `cargo-husky` (user-hooks mode) and live in `.cargo-husky/hooks/`. They install into `.git/hooks/` on the next dev-dep realization of `paigasus-helikon`. To force a re-install after editing one: `rm -rf target/debug/build/cargo-husky-* && cargo test -p paigasus-helikon --no-run`.

- **`commit-msg`** — runs `convco check --from-stdin` (enforces the `.versionrc` allowlist).
- **`pre-commit`** — intentional no-op (`exit 0`). The file exists to claim the slot so future cargo-husky upgrades don't fill it in with surprise behavior.
- **`pre-push`** — runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `convco check <merge-base>..HEAD`. Catches the three fastest CI gates pre-push; deliberately omits `cargo test` and `cargo doc` (too slow for every push). Bypass for WIP branches: `git push --no-verify`.

Three rules here are easy to get wrong, and each has already cost a debugging session:

- **The re-install silently does nothing inside a git worktree** — cargo-husky searches for a `.git` *directory* and a worktree's is a file, so it installs nothing and the old hook keeps running. Run the re-install from the **main checkout**, and verify with `grep` against the installed copy rather than assuming.
- **Never hand-copy a hook onto `.git/hooks/<name>`** — on this machine the Entire CLI owns `pre-push` and chains to `.git/hooks/pre-push.pre-entire`, which is where the cargo-husky hook actually lives. Check for a `.pre-entire` sibling first and install into that slot.
- **The convco baseline must be a merge-base, not a branch tip** — `convco check A..B` silently falls back to walking the entire history when `A` is not an ancestor of `B`, rejecting correct branches with failures the author did not write.

Mechanics and the SMA-547 postmortem: `docs/runbooks/local-hooks.md`.

## Fixture line endings

`.gitattributes` pins `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/tests/fixtures/*.txt` to `text eol=lf`. The streaming tests `include_str!` the SSE fixtures and split them on literal `\n` delimiters; without this, Windows checkouts produce CRLF bytes and the literal-string splits return one part instead of two. When adding wire-format fixtures elsewhere that the test code parses byte-level, extend the rule.

Provenance headers for wire-format fixtures follow `CONTRIBUTING.md` → "Wire-format fixtures".

- Feature branches must match the `branch-names` ruleset (`feature/**` or `hotfix/**`); a `chore/**` branch is rejected at push with `GH013 … creations being restricted`.

Full lifecycle, the 4-step recipe, and the SMA-321/SMA-346 postmortems: `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md`.

Third-party version pins live in `[workspace.dependencies]` (root). Members reference them via `dep.workspace = true`. Internal crate paths are also in `[workspace.dependencies]` so the facade can use `workspace = true` consistently.

## Non-obvious patterns to preserve

- **Feature naming**: kebab-case in `[features]` (`runtime-tokio`), snake-case in `pub use` aliases (`runtime_tokio`). They must stay paired across the facade's `Cargo.toml` and `src/lib.rs`.
- **`paigasus-helikon-cli` uses `autobins = false`** because the `paigasus-helikon` (hyphen) binary maps to `src/bin/paigasus_helikon.rs` (underscore — hyphens are illegal in Rust filenames). Removing `autobins = false` reintroduces a phantom `paigasus_helikon` binary that conflicts with the explicit `[[bin]]` entry.
- **`paigasus-helikon-macros` is a proc-macro crate from day one** (`[lib] proc-macro = true`). Don't convert it to a regular lib even though it currently has no macros.
- **The `paigasus-helikon` facade lib shares its name with the `paigasus-helikon` CLI binary by design** (Notion ref's "fully-qualified shim alias"). This produces a non-fatal `cargo doc` filename-collision warning. Don't "fix" it by renaming either — both names are user-facing API. The accepted future fix is `doc = false` on the CLI binary entry.
- **License is dual `Apache-2.0 OR MIT`** (decided 2026-05-20, reversing the 2026-05-16 MIT-only call). Both `LICENSE-APACHE` and `LICENSE-MIT` live at the repo root; the workspace metadata is `license = "Apache-2.0 OR MIT"`. Per Rust ecosystem convention — no Apache-only or MIT-only crates in the workspace. Contributions are accepted under the same dual license by default (the standard inbound-equals-outbound clause is restated in `README.md`).
- **MSRV is `1.94`** (workspace-package level; raised from 1.85 in SMA-329 because sqlx 0.9.0 declares `rust-version = "1.94.0"` — the pre-existing highest floor in the workspace). If a dep raises MSRV, bump `rust-version` to what cargo demands rather than downgrading the dep.
- **Workspace-wide `missing_docs` enforcement** lives in root `Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.lints.rust] missing_docs = "warn"`). Each non-CLI crate opts in with `[lints] workspace = true`. The CLI overrides locally with `[lints.rust] missing_docs = "allow"` and does **not** include `workspace = true` — cargo treats `[lints] workspace = true` and an inline `[lints.<tool>]` table as mutually exclusive. When adding a new crate, copy the opt-in block. When adding a new `pub use` re-export to the facade, give it a `///` doc comment or `-D warnings` will fail the docs job.
- **`cargo msrv` has no `--workspace` flag.** The msrv workflow verifies one representative inheriting crate: `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify`. Because every member uses `rust-version.workspace = true`, success on one is success on all. Don't "fix" the workflow by adding `--workspace`; that's what the first SMA-305 CI run died on.
- **Nightly is date-pinned** (`NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN: nightly-2026-05-01` at the workflow `env:` level in `ci.yml`, threaded into the doc-coverage script as `NIGHTLY_CHANNEL`). The rustdoc JSON coverage format is `-Z unstable-options` and can shift between nightlies; floating `nightly` would be a CI footgun. Bumping is a one-line follow-up chore, not an emergency.
- **Bootstrap commits on release infrastructure must use `chore(...)` or `docs(...)` types**, never `feat`/`fix`. release-plz parses every commit since the last per-crate tag — a `feat(workspace): ...` commit that touches every `Cargo.toml` would attribute a bump to every crate. The SMA-307 bootstrap PR followed this rule; the same rule applies to any future `release-plz.toml` or `release-plz.yml` edits.

## Model routing

The general tiering rules are in the global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Only the repo-specific rules are here.

- **Use Opus for release work.** This covers release-plz, the stub-ascend recipe, a hand-bumped crate version, and any red required gate. A wrong answer breaks a publish; see `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md`.
- **Haiku can read CI output.** Change to Opus when the question becomes *why* a required gate is red.

## Workflow conventions

- Branch per Linear issue: `feature/<sma-####>-<kebab-title>`. The branch name is pre-computed in each Linear ticket's `gitBranchName` field.
- Design artifacts per ticket (`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md`) land on the feature branch alongside the implementation — not pre-merged to `main`.
- **Keep the public mdBook (`docs/book/`) current — update it in the same PR as any user-facing change.** Before opening a PR, check whether the work changes public API, the quickstart/example flow, the crate roster (incl. a stub crate ascending to published), or a documented concept; if so, bring the affected `docs/book/src/*.md` page(s) into line on the same branch. The book is published from `main` and drifts silently otherwise — it sat as the untouched SMA-311 scaffold (13/17 pages still `> **Stub.**`) through all of Stage 1 before anyone noticed; SMA-423 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no book edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip. `mdbook build docs/book` must stay clean (`[output.linkcheck] warning-policy = "error"`).
- **Keep crate `README.md` files current — update the affected crate's README in the same PR as any change to its public surface.** Each of the ten published crates' `README.md` is its crates.io (and docs.rs landing-sidebar) page — no crate sets an explicit `readme`, so Cargo uses the default `README.md`. Before opening a PR, for every crate the work touches check whether the change affects that crate's public API / usage example, its install or feature story, or its published status (a stub ascending to published, a renamed/added feature flag); if so, bring its `crates/<crate>/README.md` into line on the same branch — and also the facade `crates/paigasus-helikon/README.md` and the root `README.md` whenever the crate roster or the feature → module map changes. README install snippets deliberately use drift-free `cargo add` (no hardcoded versions), so a routine version bump alone needs no README edit. Like the mdBook, the READMEs drift silently otherwise — they sat as untouched 3-line SMA-304 stubs (`Stub — see SMA-304`) through all of Stage 1 while ten crates shipped real implementations; SMA-424 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no README edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip.
- Commit prefix: `<type>(<scope>): SMA-### <message>` (e.g. `feat(facade): SMA-304 ...`).
- **PR titles must satisfy two independent rules from `pr-title.yml`** (`amannn/action-semantic-pull-request`):
  1. **Full Conventional Commits format.** The action enforces a valid `type(scope):` prefix from the action's configured `types` list — independent of the subject regex. `SMA-317 add anthropic provider` (no prefix) fails; `feat(providers-anthropic): SMA-317 add anthropic provider` passes.
  2. **Subject must start lowercase after the `SMA-###` prefix.** The `subjectPattern: ^([A-Z]{2,4}-\d+ )?[^A-Z].+$` rejects `feat(core): SMA-314 LlmAgent + ...` because `L` is uppercase; lead the subject with a lowercase verb (`add`, `wire`, `pin`, `promote`, `implement`, `fix`).
  Per-commit Conventional Commit titles on the feature branch don't trip either rule — only the PR title (which becomes the squashed `main` commit) is gated.
- Linear auto-closes the linked SMA-* issue when its PR merges; no manual status move needed.
- **Always implement GitHub Actions against the latest stable major**, pinned to a commit SHA (never a moving `@vN` tag), keeping the human-readable version as a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment **on the `uses:` line**, so the SHA is auditable. The comment must end with the version: Dependabot updates only a same-line comment that ends with the old version, so a version on its own line above the step goes stale on every bump (SMA-744). This rule applies only to pins of a tagged release. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is pinned to an untagged `master` commit, so it has no version comment. Do not add one, because no tag gives a correct version. The `gh-actions` Dependabot group sets no `update-types`, so its configuration permits major bumps in the same grouped PR. Do not depend on that: `actions/checkout` still sat on v6.0.2 until SMA-486 bumped it by hand, so **check for a new major by hand**. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is a special case: it ships rolling branches and a periodically re-pointed `v1` tag, so confirm the direction (`ahead_by > 0, behind_by == 0`) before accepting any bump — the naive "bump to latest release" recipe once would have proposed an ~11-month downgrade. Independently and permanently: every site pinning it **must** pair the SHA with an explicit `with: toolchain: …`, because a SHA ref carries no toolchain selector. Recipes and history: `docs/runbooks/github-actions-pinning.md`.
- **After a PR merges to `main`, release-plz opens/updates a `chore: release` PR** (authored by the paigasusbot App) carrying the version bumps + CHANGELOG; in the normal flow **merging that PR is what publishes to crates.io** (the merged feature PR left versions matching the registry, so its own `main` push publishes nothing). The exception is a PR that bumps its own version — the stub-ascend ritual — which publishes on its own merge with no separate release PR. Check the release PR after every merge and watch its CI — its release-PR `cargo update` can pull a fresh advisory that reddens `audit`/`deny` on the bot PR **only** (independent of `main`); fix with a `chore(deps)` pin and release-plz regenerates the PR clean.

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs nine jobs on every PR (`commits` is PR-only; the other eight also run on push to `main`): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test` (matrix `{ubuntu, macos, windows} × {stable, 1.94}`, `fail-fast: false`), `build-no-default-features`, `docs` (`RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`), `doc-coverage` (gated at `DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD`, default 80%), `commits` (`convco check`), `sessions-it` (Postgres/Redis, path-filtered), and `markdown-lint`. The `paigasus-helikon-cli` crate is excluded from both the `missing_docs` lint and the coverage aggregator until its public API stabilizes.

`.github/workflows/integration.yml` runs `temporal-it` and `agentcore-image` as **signal-only** jobs, deliberately outside `ci.yml` so an expected flake cannot make "ci is red on `main`" meaningless. **Signal-only means *not listed as required*, never `continue-on-error`.**

`.github/workflows/msrv.yml` runs `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify` as a non-required signal that the declared MSRV is truthful.

Supply-chain workflows (`audit.yml`, `deny.yml`, `sbom.yml`) are separate from `ci.yml` because they have independent triggers and failure semantics. `audit.yml` and `deny.yml` both run on push to `main`, PRs, a daily cron, and `workflow_dispatch`, so `main` is re-evaluated daily at exactly PR severity.

**To read an audit verdict, use the Checks API, not the legacy commit-status API** — the latter returns only `CodeRabbit` on this repo, rendering a confident `state: success` that contains no audit verdict whatsoever:

```bash
gh api repos/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/commits/main/check-runs \
  --jq '.check_runs[] | select(.name=="audit" or .name=="deny") | {name, status, conclusion}'
```

Note also that the `scheduled-audit` job's green status means nothing at any severity — read the *run* conclusion, never that job's status.

The required-status-check contexts gated on `main` are (bare job names, as posted by the GitHub Actions app): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test (ubuntu-latest, stable)`, `test (macos-latest, stable)`, `test (windows-latest, stable)`, `docs`, `doc-coverage`, `book-build`, `commits`, `pr-title`, `audit`, `deny`, `sessions-it`, `build-no-default-features`, `markdown-lint`. The macOS job is required because it is the only gate that compiles and runs the Seatbelt backend; the Windows job because it is the only gate that exercises the Windows timeout path in `paigasus-helikon-tools` — `cmd /C` process spawning and a `TerminateProcess`-based kill, which unlike the unix path has no process-group semantics and assigns a real exit code (SMA-569); `sessions-it` because it is the only gate that runs the live Postgres/Redis session backends; `build-no-default-features` because it is the only gate that compiles `runtime-axum` and `runtime-actix` with default features off. The canonical declaration is `.github/rulesets/main-protection-checks.json` (see CONTRIBUTING.md → "Repo configuration"). Other matrix variants (the `1.94` legs) run as signals only.

These pins are hand-bumped with nothing tracking them: `TEMPORAL_CLI_VERSION`/`TEMPORAL_CLI_SHA256` in `integration.yml`, `NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN` in `ci.yml`, `convco@…` in `ci.yml`'s `commits` job, `MDBOOK_VERSION`/`MDBOOK_LINKCHECK_VERSION` in `docs.yml`, and `markdownlint-cli2` via `package-lock.json`. **A checksum mismatch is never a signal to update the digest** — the causes are, in order, a truncated download, an upstream re-tag, and tampering; verify upstream independently first.

**The workspace needs no system `protoc`** (SMA-623): `temporalio-client`'s `vendored-protox` feature compiles the Temporal protos with `protox`. `ci.yml` sets `PROTOC` to a path that does not exist, and `build-no-default-features` asserts that the feature is active. If a build fails with "Could not find `protoc`", do not add a `protoc` install — find which build script calls it. Rationale and recovery: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "protoc and protox".

Job-by-job rationale, the audit/deny signal semantics, and the incident history behind all of the above: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md`.

**GitHub's 10 GB Actions cache limit is a standing constraint, not a one-time cleanup** (SMA-618): it is GitHub's **default**, not a hard ceiling — a repo admin, org owner or enterprise owner can raise it (user-owned repos up to 10 TB) at additional storage cost, and SMA-618 deliberately chose to fit inside it rather than pay. Enforced at 10 **GiB** (10,737,418,240 bytes) despite the "10 GB" wording. Going over fails nothing — it just triggers silent LRU eviction that makes CI legs run cold at random. `cache-budget.yml` monitors it daily and warns (never fails) above 8.5 GiB. Caches are saved **only** from `main` (`save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}` on every `Swatinem/rust-cache` site) so a PR job can still restore an entry `main` wrote but never writes a competing `refs/pull/N/merge` entry that evicts it. The `CARGO_*`/`RUST*`-prefixed workflow env that `rust-cache` hashes into its key must stay byte-identical across every cache-bearing workflow, enforced by `scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh` running as a step in `fmt`. `audit` and `deny` deliberately cache no `target/` directory — neither compiles the workspace, so it was pure waste against the fixed budget.  CI also sets **`CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only`** (SMA-618 PR 2), which measured a **16.5% cut in total cache bytes** — 14-29% on the `test` legs and exactly 0% on `clippy`/`docs`/`doc-coverage`, which are metadata-mode builds with no debug info to remove. (A local sample of the largest `.rlib` files suggested 79%; do not extrapolate an aggregate from its densest component.) Keeping line tables preserves file:line in panic backtraces. Like `CARGO_TERM_COLOR`, it is **inside** rust-cache's key, so it must be byte-identical in every cache-bearing workflow — adding it to one and not the rest silently splits the cache rather than failing. `prefix-key: v1` marks the post-PR-2 generation, so any surviving `v0-` entry is provably stale and safe to purge — note it **replaces** the default `v0-rust` entirely, so keys read `v1-<job>-...`, not `v1-rust-<job>-...`. `clippy` and `docs` share one entry via `shared-key: metadata`, with `clippy` the sole writer and `docs` carrying a literal `save-if: false`; exactly one site may save a shared key, and the guard enforces it. Full rationale: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "Actions cache budget".

The **`microvm`/forkd live-KVM path is not validated locally or in GitHub CI** — the dev host is arm64 macOS (no `/dev/kvm`) and GitHub runners have none. Validate it on a **GCP nested-virtualization VM** (Ubuntu 24.04 — the forkd binaries need glibc ≥ 2.38; Intel `n2`) per `docs/runbooks/forkd-live-validation.md`. The `tests/forkd_live.rs` tests are env-gated (`FORKD_URL` / `FORKD_TOKEN` / `FORKD_SNAPSHOT`) and loud-skip when no controller is configured, so `cargo test` stays green without one.

## Local hooks

Hooks are managed via `cargo-husky` (user-hooks mode) and live in `.cargo-husky/hooks/`. They install into `.git/hooks/` on the next dev-dep realization of `paigasus-helikon`. To force a re-install after editing one: `rm -rf target/debug/build/cargo-husky-* && cargo test -p paigasus-helikon --no-run`.

- **`commit-msg`** — runs `convco check --from-stdin` (enforces the `.versionrc` allowlist).
- **`pre-commit`** — intentional no-op (`exit 0`). The file exists to claim the slot so future cargo-husky upgrades don't fill it in with surprise behavior.
- **`pre-push`** — runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `convco check <merge-base>..HEAD`. Catches the three fastest CI gates pre-push; deliberately omits `cargo test` and `cargo doc` (too slow for every push). Bypass for WIP branches: `git push --no-verify`.

Three rules here are easy to get wrong, and each has already cost a debugging session:

- **The re-install silently does nothing inside a git worktree** — cargo-husky searches for a `.git` *directory* and a worktree's is a file, so it installs nothing and the old hook keeps running. Run the re-install from the **main checkout**, and verify with `grep` against the installed copy rather than assuming.
- **Never hand-copy a hook onto `.git/hooks/<name>`** — on this machine the Entire CLI owns `pre-push` and chains to `.git/hooks/pre-push.pre-entire`, which is where the cargo-husky hook actually lives. Check for a `.pre-entire` sibling first and install into that slot.
- **The convco baseline must be a merge-base, not a branch tip** — `convco check A..B` silently falls back to walking the entire history when `A` is not an ancestor of `B`, rejecting correct branches with failures the author did not write.

Mechanics and the SMA-547 postmortem: `docs/runbooks/local-hooks.md`.

## Fixture line endings

`.gitattributes` pins `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/tests/fixtures/*.txt` to `text eol=lf`. The streaming tests `include_str!` the SSE fixtures and split them on literal `\n` delimiters; without this, Windows checkouts produce CRLF bytes and the literal-string splits return one part instead of two. When adding wire-format fixtures elsewhere that the test code parses byte-level, extend the rule.

Provenance headers for wire-format fixtures follow `CONTRIBUTING.md` → "Wire-format fixtures".

  ## Verdict: APPROVE WITH CHANGES

  ### BLOCKER
  None
  
  ### MAJOR

    - `drop_thinking_without_own_block` clears the slots of a lost group (`translate/request.rs:552-566`).
    - `into_output` removes the thinking from the last assistant message and clears the slots (`request.rs:527-532`).

Every multi-text response with tool calls then reaches the lost-group path. The API accepts adjacent text blocks, so nothing fails. But the invariant breaks silently, because every existing test uses `text_pos` with no `len` and takes the fallback. | Suggested fix: build one text `WireBlock` that carries its split plan (piece keys and byte ranges), with the key of the first position. Expand it in `WireMessage::into_value` after `drop_thinking_without_own_block`, and only while the block still has a slot. The last message and lost groups then keep one joined block, as today. The keep rule does not change, because a concatenation is blank only when every piece is blank. Add replay tests with `len` data for a hand-off transcript, for lost calls, and for a last assistant message. Each test asserts `messages(&items) == messages(&without_anthropic(&items))`.

Stream data gives the same order both ways, because blocks stop in index order and the `waiting_positions` flush keeps queue order (`stream.rs:314-317`). Hand-built or reordered parts can differ. Take positions `[(3,len 1),(1,len 1)]` in part order and the text `"AB"`. Then state "cut in part order". Also fall back when a `Text` index is the same as a `Block` or `ToolUse` index of the message, because equal keys sort in no defined order.

They do not show that the guard, and not some other cause, stops the split. Also not covered:
    - The drop paths above.
    - The stream shapes that make the sum fall short: a text block whose stop never arrives, a `text_delta` for an index that is not open (`stream.rs:142-144` emits `TokenDelta` for any index), a block stop after the terminal event (`stream.rs:243-250`), and a repeated `content_block_start` that resets the counter.
    - Text before the first kept thinking block, end to end: `[Text A(0), Thinking(1), Text B(2), ToolUse(3)]` must replay as `[A, Th1, B, tu3]`.
    - An empty first text block, `[Th0, Text ""(1), tu2, Th3, Text "B"(4), tu5]`. Today "B" goes to index 1. The new code puts it at index 4. This is a real fix, and the test is red on today's code.
    - A positive multi-byte split, for example `"é"` and `"ü"`.
    - The "more than one text part" fallback. The spec lists this case but has no test for it.
    - The multi-text shape in `session_projection_round_trip` (`translate/mod.rs:1337`).

Say that an equal-length edit splits and that this is harmless.
  - **A dropped blank piece changes the replayed bytes and leaves one shape unfixed** - In `[Th0, Text "\n\n"(1), Th2, Text "B"(3)]` the blank piece is dropped, so `Th2` still has a changed prefix. Today's joined replay sends the `"\n\n"`. The split replay does not. This is not a regression: I found no shape where today keeps a thinking block that the split loses. | Suggested fix: write this down as a known limit, so the decision is on record.
  - **Stored `len` values are untrusted, and the spec does not forbid a panic** - The spec checks only char boundaries. A stored `len` of `u64::MAX` overflows the sum: a debug build panics, and a release build wraps.   - **The rollback and release facts are not stated** - The old code reads new data safely. `AnthropicData` has no `deny_unknown_fields` (`provider_data.rs:75-77`), and `text_seen` takes the first position (`request.rs:702`). But after a downgrade, a later thinking block whose signature includes the split prefix gets dropped one time under `drop_block`. SMA-840 has not shipped yet: the CHANGELOG lists it nowhere, and 0.3.1 holds only a core update (`CHANGELOG.md:8-14`). So "old data without `len`" exists only for users who build from `main`. | Suggested fix: add a short rollout note. Keep `Option<u64>`, because it costs little. Now, before the first release writes this shape into stored sessions, is the cheapest time to set the field name. Consider `bytes`, or document `len` as "UTF-8 bytes".
  - **In-code docs that the spec does not list** - These say "first text block": the module doc at `request.rs:7-12`, the comments at `request.rs:701` and `729-730`, and the `AnthropicData::Text` doc at `provider_data.rs:85`. The spec's book reference is `docs/book/src/concepts/model-providers.md`, not `model-providers.md`. Separately, the core `ModelTurn` doc (`core/src/model.rs:573-575`) says "text, reasoning and/or provider data, in that order", but `build_items` puts `Reasoning` first (`model.rs:627-633`). The spec repeats this incorrect order. The design does not depend on the order, so this is only a doc fix.
  
  ### QUESTIONS
  - Did a live probe show that today's joined replay drops `Thinking(2)`, and that the split replay keeps it? The SMA-840 table covers "inserted a text block before the thinking block", not "text joined across a thinking block". The SMA-840 non-goal (`...sma-840...-design.md:121-122`) also says "Probe finding 4 shows the API does not check order", which disagrees with this spec.   - Text blocks with citations: the parser skips `citations_delta` (an unknown variant makes the event fail to parse, and the event is skipped), so the replay sends the text with no citations. That probably still changes the prefix. Is this a known limit to record?
  
  ## What's good
  - The sum check validates itself. Each source of extra `TokenDelta` bytes makes the sum fall short, so the translator falls back to today's bytes with no special code. Examples are synthesized JSON (`stream.rs:166-168`), deltas for an index that is not open, missing stops, stops after the terminal event, and backends that normalize text. Add a test with `len: u64::MAX`.

## Prefix check (added after the local review)

### Facts

Two live probes on 2026-11-21 and the Claude API reference gave these facts.

- Newer models run a history-editing check, also called the prefix check. These models are Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Haiku 5.5, and Fable 5.1 and 5.2.
- A signature of a thinking block records the top-level `system` text, the `tools` set, and every message before the block. It also records a chain to the previous thinking block. A client can remove blocks from the front of the history. A client cannot remove blocks from the middle.
- Accounts made on or after 2026-08-31 get an HTTP 400 when the prefix changed. The message is `messages.1.content.0: Invalid signature in thinking block. The block is bound to a different conversation.`
- The request field `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior: "drop_block"` needs the beta header `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01`. The API then drops the first mismatched block and every later thinking block. The request proceeds. The response has a top-level `input_transformations` array.
- The API accepts `block_binding` only with `thinking.type: "adaptive"`. No model accepts it with `"enabled"`. Models that do not run the check also accept the object. A request with `block_binding` and no beta header gets a 400.
- `claude-sonnet-4-5` is deprecated and retires on 2026-11-30. `Enabled { budget_tokens }` works on models before 4.6, for example `claude-haiku-4-5`. It works, deprecated, on Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6. Opus 4.7, 4.8, 5 and 5.5, Sonnet 5 and 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable reject it with a 400.

### Probe result (claude-sonnet-5-5, drop_block)

| Change before the second request | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Changed `system` | thinking block dropped |
| Added a tool | thinking block dropped |
| Changed a tool description | thinking block dropped |
| Changed the text of the first user message | thinking block dropped |
| Inserted a text block before the thinking block in the same message | thinking block dropped |
| Edited or removed text after the thinking block in the same message | thinking block kept |
| Unchanged tool loop | thinking block kept |

### Decision

Sven chose Option A. With `ExtendedThinking::Adaptive`, the provider sends `block_binding` with `prefix_mismatch_behavior: "drop_block"` and the beta header `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01`. The provider adds the header once, also when the user added it with `.beta(...)`. The provider sets extended thinking on the builder only, so the header follows the builder value. `Enabled` and `Disabled` send no binding.

Sven rejected two other options. A prefix hash is complex and needs a byte-exact copy of the request prefix. Documentation only leaves the 400 error in place for hand-offs.

With `Adaptive`, a changed prefix costs the model its earlier reasoning. The request does not fail.

# SMA-854: one position for each Anthropic text block

Linear: [SMA-854](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-854). Approach approved by
Sven on 2026-11-22. Revised after the adversarial challenge on the same day.

## Intent

The Anthropic stream records a position only for the first text block of a
response (`stream.rs`, `text_position_recorded`). The request translator gives
all text of the turn that one position (`translate/request.rs`, `text_seen`).
When a thinking block is between two text blocks, the replay changes the block
order:

- Response: `[Thinking(0), Text "A"(1), Thinking(2), Text "B"(3), ToolUse(4)]`
- Replay today: `[Thinking(0), Text "AB", Thinking(2), ToolUse(4)]`

With `ExtendedThinking::Adaptive` the provider sends `drop_block`. The models
that run the prefix check then drop `Thinking(2)` and every later thinking
block. The request does not fail, but the model loses that reasoning.

The goal: the replay sends the text blocks of such a response at their own
positions, so the block order is the same as in the response.

### Evidence for the bug

The SMA-840 design has two statements that disagree. Its non-goal says "Probe
finding 4 shows the API does not check order". Its later prefix-check probe
table (`2026-11-21-sma-840-anthropic-thinking-signatures-design.md`, "Probe
result") says that "Inserted a text block before the thinking block in the same
message" makes the API drop the thinking block. The joined `"AB"` before
`Thinking(2)` is a change of that kind. So the bug is probable. No live probe
has yet sent this exact shape.

## Facts that set the design

- The core joins all `TokenDelta` texts of a turn into one `ContentPart::Text`
  with `push_str` and no separator (`paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:701`).
  No `ModelEvent` marks a text block boundary. `build_items` gives at most one
  `AssistantMessage`, with the parts `[Reasoning?, Text?, ProviderData*]`.
- The stream emits position records only after it keeps a thinking block
  (`position`, `waiting_positions`). A response with no kept thinking block
  writes no provider data, so its replay does not change.
- `AnthropicData` is `pub(crate)`. The `data` shape is private to the crate
  (`provider_data.rs` module doc, book `docs/book/src/concepts/model-providers.md:134`).
- The keep rule contract (`request.rs:220-228`): when a rule fails, the thinking
  blocks are dropped, and the item builds as if it had no Anthropic part. The
  SMA-840 tests check this with `without_anthropic` equality.
- SMA-840 is merged on `main` but not yet released. So stored data with a `text`
  position exists only for users who build from `main`.

## Goals

- The stream records one position for each text block of a response.
- The replay sends each text block at its own position, when the thinking
  blocks of that response are sent.
- When the thinking blocks are not sent, the message builds exactly as it does
  today: one joined text block.
- Stored data from before this change still replays as it does today.

## Non-goals

- No change to `paigasus-helikon-core`, to `ModelEvent`, or to the "at most one
  `Text` part" behaviour of the core.
- No change for other providers.
- No change to a response with no kept thinking block.
- No live probe in this ticket (see "Open question for Sven").

## Approaches

1. **Chosen: record the byte length of each text block, and cut the joined text
   on replay.** The change is only in the Anthropic crate. When the stored
   lengths do not match the text, the translator falls back to the behaviour of
   today.
2. **A core event for text block boundaries, so that the core makes several
   `Text` parts.** Rejected. It changes the core contract, needs a breaking
   bump of the core with a cascade to all dependent crates, and touches every

- The `Text` indexes, in part order, are strictly increasing.
- No `Text` index is the same as a `Block` or `ToolUse` index of the message.
- The sum of `bytes` is the byte length of the text part. The sum uses
  `checked_add` and `usize::try_from`. An overflow means "not splittable".

  never panics.

- An edit that keeps the byte length of the text (for example `John` to
  `XXXX`) still splits. This is harmless: the pieces are contiguous slices, so
  their join is always the edited text.

  thinking block. Then the later thinking blocks can be dropped, as today.

  changed prefix. Today has the same result.

  with citations goes back with no citations. That probably changes the
  prefix. This is outside this ticket.

  `deny_unknown_fields`, and the old `text_seen` logic takes the first position.

  `drop_block`. The request does not fail.

  name.

correct `bytes` values, and it splits. So each guard is proved to be the cause.

- `[Thinking, Text, Thinking, Text, ToolUse]` emits one `Text` position with
  the correct `bytes` for each text block, after the first kept block.

- A `text_delta` for an index that is not open adds to no count.
- The existing single-text tests get the `bytes` field.

Data:

- The documented shapes test includes `bytes`.
- Data with no `bytes` parses.

- The issue example replays as

- Text before the first kept thinking block:
  `[Text A(0), Thinking(1), Text B(2), ToolUse(3)]` replays in that order.
- An empty first text block: `[Th0, Text ""(1), tu2, Th3, Text "B"(4), tu5]`.
  Today `"B"` goes to index 1. The new code puts it at index 4. This test is red
  on today's code.
- A multi-byte split, for example `"é"` and `"ü"`.
- A blank piece gives no block.
- The existing test `two_text_blocks_join_at_first_text_position`
  (`translate/mod.rs:1277`) is renamed and inverted: the two blocks split.
- The multi-text shape in `session_projection_round_trip`
  (`translate/mod.rs:1337`) is checked against the new result.
- A round trip through `ModelTurnAccumulator` (the `items_of` helper in
  `translate/mod.rs`) from the stream to the request.

Replay, fallback (each with its control):

- A sum mismatch.
- A missing `bytes`.
- A cut that is not on a `char` boundary.
- `Text` indexes that are not strictly increasing.
- A `Text` index that is the same as a `Block` or `ToolUse` index.
- More than one non-blank text part.
- A `bytes` of `u64::MAX`: no panic, and a fallback.
- Hand-built events with synthesized structured output: the sum is short, so a
  fallback. (The API rejects a forced `tool_choice` with thinking on, so a live
  test cannot make this shape.)

Replay, drop paths (each asserts
`messages(&items) == messages(&without_anthropic(&items))` with `bytes` data):

- A hand-off transcript that removed the tool calls.
- A history that lost the tool calls.
- A last assistant message.

## Docs and release

- No public API change. A `fix(providers)` commit gives the Anthropic crate a
  patch bump through release-plz, with the facade cascade.
- In-code docs that say "first text block" change: the module doc of
  `request.rs` (lines 7-12), the comments at `request.rs:701` and `729-730`, and
  the `AnthropicData::Text` doc (`provider_data.rs:85`).
- The book (`docs/book/src/concepts/model-providers.md:139`) already says that
  an edit of an earlier message makes the API drop the thinking. That still
  covers the fallback cases, so the book needs no change.
- The crate README describes the keep rule, not the text position. It needs no
  change.

## Open question for Sven

A live probe could confirm the bug and the fix. It needs a real response with
the shape `[Thinking, Text, Thinking, Text]`, which adaptive thinking makes only
sometimes. The API reports a dropped block in `input_transformations`, so an
env-gated live test could observe it.

## Left to the builder

- The exact names of new helper functions and of the split plan type.
- The place of the cut logic (a small pure function next to
  `assistant_blocks` is expected).

# SMA-854: one position for each Anthropic text block

Linear: [SMA-854](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-854). Status: approved by Sven on 2026-11-22.

## Intent

The Anthropic stream records a position only for the first text block of a
response (`stream.rs`, `text_position_recorded`). The request translator gives
all text of the turn that one position (`translate/request.rs`, `text_seen`).
When a thinking block is between two text blocks, the replay changes the block
order:

- Response: `[Thinking(0), Text "A"(1), Thinking(2), Text "B"(3), ToolUse(4)]`
- Replay today: `[Thinking(0), Text "AB", Thinking(2), ToolUse(4)]`

With `ExtendedThinking::Adaptive` the provider sends `drop_block`. The models
that run the prefix check then drop `Thinking(2)` and every later thinking
block. The request does not fail, but the model loses that reasoning.

The goal: the replay sends the text blocks of such a response at their own
positions, so the block order is the same as in the response.

## Facts that set the design

- The core joins all `TokenDelta` texts of a turn into one `ContentPart::Text`
  with `push_str` and no separator (`paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:701`).
  No `ModelEvent` marks a text block boundary. The `ModelTurn` doc says a turn
  gives at most one `AssistantMessage`, with text, reasoning and provider data
  in that order.
- The stream emits position records only after it keeps a thinking block
  (`position`, `waiting_positions`). A response with no kept thinking block
  writes no provider data, so its replay does not change.
- `AnthropicData` is `pub(crate)`. The `data` shape is private to the crate
  (`provider_data.rs` module doc, book `model-providers.md:134`).

## Goals

- The stream records one position for each text block of a response.
- The replay sends each text block at its own position.
- Stored data from before this change still replays as it does today.

## Non-goals

- No change to `paigasus-helikon-core`, to `ModelEvent`, or to the "at most one
  `Text` part" behaviour of the core.
- No change for other providers.
- No change to a response with no kept thinking block.

## Approaches

1. **Chosen: record the byte length of each text block, and cut the joined text
   on replay.** The change is only in the Anthropic crate. When the stored
   lengths do not match the text, the translator falls back to the behaviour of
   today.
2. **A core event for text block boundaries, so that the core makes several
   `Text` parts.** Rejected. It changes the core contract, needs a breaking
   bump of the core with a cascade to all dependent crates, and touches every
   provider. That is too much for a rare shape with Low priority.
3. **Keep one joined text block at a different position.** Rejected. Any
   position for the joined text still changes the order before `Thinking(2)`.

## Design

### Stream (`stream.rs`)

- Remove `text_position_recorded`. On each `content_block_stop` of a text block,
  emit `AnthropicData::Text { index, len }` through `position` (so it waits for
  the first kept thinking block, as today).
- `len` is the UTF-8 byte length of all `text_delta` texts of that block. The
  `BlockState::Text` variant counts it. The stream already sends the same texts
  as `TokenDelta`, so the sum of all `len` values is the byte length of the
  text that the core joins, when no other `TokenDelta` source is in the turn.

### Data shape (`provider_data.rs`)

- `AnthropicData::Text` gets `len: Option<u64>` with `#[serde(default,
  skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`. New data:
  `{"kind":"text","index":3,"len":5}`. Older data with no `len` still parses.

### Replay (`translate/request.rs`, `assistant_blocks`)

- Collect all `Text` positions of the message in part order.
- The message is **splittable** when all of these are true:
  - It has exactly one non-blank `ContentPart::Text` part.
  - Every `Text` position has a `len`.
  - The sum of the `len` values is the byte length of that text part.
  - Each cut falls on a `char` boundary.
- When the message is splittable, cut the text into one piece per position, in
  position order. Each piece becomes its own `text` block with the key
  `SortKey::At(index, 1)`. A blank piece gives no block, because the API
  rejects a blank text block.
- When the message is not splittable, do what the translator does today: every
  text part gets the key of the first `Text` position, or
  `SortKey::BeforeFirstToolUse` when there is none.
- Adjacent text blocks of the response stay separate blocks. This sends the
  same block structure as the response.

### Cases that fall back to today

- A host edited the text of the assistant message.
- The data is from before this change (no `len`).
- The turn had structured output: the synthesized tool JSON also goes into the
  joined text as `TokenDelta`, so the sum does not match.
- A message has more than one text part (a host built it by hand).

## Tests (TDD)

- Stream: a response `[Thinking, Text, Thinking, Text, ToolUse]` emits a
  `Text` position with the correct `len` for each text block, after the first
  kept block. Multi-byte UTF-8 text counts bytes.
- Stream: the existing single-text tests get the `len` field.
- Data: the documented shapes test includes `len`, and data with no `len`
  parses.
- Replay: the issue example replays as
  `[Thinking(0), Text "A", Thinking(2), Text "B", ToolUse(4)]`.
- Replay fallback: a length mismatch, a missing `len`, and a cut that is not on
  a `char` boundary each give the result of today.
- Replay: a blank piece gives no block.
- A round trip through `ModelTurnAccumulator` (the `items_of` helper in
  `translate/mod.rs`) from the stream to the request.

## Docs and release

- No public API change. A `fix(providers)` commit gives the Anthropic crate a
  patch bump through release-plz, with the facade cascade.
- The book (`model-providers.md:139`) already says that an edit of an earlier
  message makes the API drop the thinking. That still covers the fallback
  cases, so the book needs no change.
- The crate README describes the keep rule, not the text position. It needs no
  change.

## Left to the builder

- The exact names of new helper functions.
- The place of the cut logic (a small function next to `assistant_blocks` is
  expected).

The permission system blocked the check for an API key, and that is correct. I do not try a different way to read it. The live probe stays an open question for Sven.

## GATE 1: spec approval

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-22-anthropic-per-text-block-positions-design.md` (in the worktree, not committed yet).

**Challenger verdict: APPROVE WITH CHANGES.** It found 0 blockers, 3 major findings and 6 minor findings. It confirmed that the core idea is sound: the sum check validates itself, and old data and unknown shapes fall back to the behaviour of today.

**What I changed in the spec:**

| Finding | Change |
|---|---|
| MAJOR: the split survives the drop paths. This breaks the SMA-840 rule "builds as if it had no Anthropic part" for hand-off transcripts and for the last message. | The text stays **one** block that carries a split plan. It expands in `into_value` only after the drop pass, and only while it still has a slot. Hand-off, lost calls and the last message build exactly as today. |
| MAJOR: the cut order is ambiguous, so text can be reordered. | New splittable conditions: the `Text` indexes must be strictly increasing, and no index can be equal to a thinking or `tool_use` index. |
| MAJOR: the fallback tests pass on today's code. | Each fallback test now has a control test that does split. I added tests for the drop paths, for text before the first thinking block, and for an empty first text block (red today). The existing `two_text_blocks_join…` test is inverted. |
| MINOR: a stored length can panic (`u64::MAX`). | Checked arithmetic and `str::get`, with a `u64::MAX` test. |
| MINOR: no log on a fallback. | A `debug!` line gives the reason and the lengths only, never the content. |
| MINOR: the field name, and the rollout. | The field is renamed `bytes`. A rollout note says that SMA-840 is not released, so now is the cheapest time to set the name. |
| MINOR: the fallback list was incorrect. | An edit that keeps the byte length still splits, and that is harmless. The blank-piece case and the `citations_delta` case are now recorded as known limits. |
| MINOR: some in-code docs still say "first text block". | Added to the docs list. |

**Rejected:**

- *Fix the core `ModelTurn` doc order ("text, reasoning", but the code puts reasoning first).* This is correct, but it touches the core crate, which gives a core release and a cascade. It is outside this ticket. I can file a separate Linear issue if you want.

**Open questions for you:**

1. **A live probe.** No one has sent this exact shape to the API. The SMA-840 spec also contradicts itself on whether the API checks the order. But the later SMA-840 probe ("a text block inserted before the thinking block → dropped") makes the bug probable. A probe needs a real `[Thinking, Text, Thinking, Text]` response, and adaptive thinking makes that shape only sometimes. I recommend that we ship without a probe, because the fix is safe also if the API does not check the order. Do you want an env-gated live test anyway?
2. **The core doc fix.** Should I file it as a separate issue?

Please approve the spec, ask for changes, or ask for a new challenge run.

"""SMA-854 live probe. Reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the environment.

Prints block types, HTTP status, and input_transformations only. Never prints
the key or a signature. Raw responses go to OUT_DIR for fixture transcription.
"""
import json
import os
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

KEY = os.environ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"]
MODEL = os.environ.get("PROBE_MODEL", "claude-sonnet-5-5")
OUT_DIR = sys.argv[1]
ATTEMPTS = int(os.environ.get("PROBE_ATTEMPTS", "6"))

TOOLS = [
    {
        "name": "lookup_city_code",
        "description": "Return the internal code for a city. You need the code before you can get the weather.",
        "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]},
    },
    {
        "name": "weather_by_code",
        "description": "Get the weather for an internal city code.",
        "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"code": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["code"]},
    },
]

PROMPTS = [
    "Before you do anything, write one short sentence to me that says your plan. Then think carefully "
    "about which city codes might exist. Then write a second short sentence to me. Then call "
    "lookup_city_code for Paris.",
    "Answer in two separate parts with thinking in between: first tell me in one sentence what 17*23 is, "
    "then think again about whether Paris or Lyon is larger, then tell me that in one sentence, then call "
    "lookup_city_code for the larger city.",
    "Write a one-line greeting. Then reason step by step about the weather tool chain. Then write a "
    "one-line summary of your reasoning. Then call lookup_city_code for Paris.",
]


def call(messages, label):
    body = {
        "model": MODEL,
        "max_tokens": 8000,
        "thinking": {"type": "adaptive", "block_binding": {"prefix_mismatch_behavior": "drop_block"}},
        "output_config": {"effort": "max"},
        "tools": TOOLS,
        "messages": messages,
    }
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        "https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages",
        data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
        headers={
            "x-api-key": KEY,
            "anthropic-version": "2023-06-01",
            "anthropic-beta": "thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01",
            "content-type": "application/json",
        },
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=300) as r:
            status, data = r.status, json.loads(r.read())
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        status, data = e.code, json.loads(e.read() or b"{}")
    with open(os.path.join(OUT_DIR, f"{label}.json"), "w") as f:
        json.dump({"request_messages": messages, "status": status, "response": data}, f, indent=1)
    return status, data


def shape(content):
    out = []
    for b in content:
        t = b.get("type")
        if t == "text":
            out.append(f"text({len(b['text'].encode())}B)")
        elif t == "thinking":
            out.append(f"thinking({len(b.get('thinking', ''))}ch)")
        else:
            out.append(t)
    return out


def interleaved(content):
    """True when a thinking block follows a text block."""
    seen_text = False
    for b in content:
        if b["type"] == "text":
            seen_text = True
        elif b["type"] in ("thinking", "redacted_thinking") and seen_text:
            return True
    return False


def report(label, status, data):
    if status != 200:
        print(f"{label}: HTTP {status} {data.get('error', {}).get('message', '')[:300]}")
        return
    print(f"{label}: 200 stop={data.get('stop_reason')} shape={shape(data['content'])} "
          f"input_transformations={json.dumps(data.get('input_transformations'))}")


def main():
    found = None
    n = 0
    for attempt in range(ATTEMPTS):
        for pi, prompt in enumerate(PROMPTS):
            n += 1
            label = f"elicit_{attempt}_{pi}"
            msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]
            status, data = call(msgs, label)
            report(label, status, data)
            if status == 200 and interleaved(data["content"]) and data.get("stop_reason") == "tool_use":
                found = (msgs, data)
                break
        if found:
            break
    if not found:
        print(f"no interleaved shape in {n} attempts")
        return
    msgs, data = found
    content = data["content"]
    tool_results = [
        {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": b["id"], "content": "PAR-7351"}
        for b in content if b["type"] == "tool_use"
    ]
    user2 = {"role": "user", "content": tool_results}

    # a) exact replay: the split replay of the fix.
    s, d = call(msgs + [{"role": "assistant", "content": content}, user2], "replay_exact")
    report("replay_exact", s, d)

    # b) joined replay: what today's translator sends. All text joined at the
    # first text position.
    texts = "".join(b["text"] for b in content if b["type"] == "text")
    joined, placed = [], False
    for b in content:
        if b["type"] == "text":
            if not placed:
                joined.append({"type": "text", "text": texts})
                placed = True
        else:
            joined.append(b)
    s, d = call(msgs + [{"role": "assistant", "content": joined}, user2], "replay_joined")
    report("replay_joined", s, d)

    # c) a whitespace-only text block in the assistant message, after the first text.
    blank = []
    for b in content:
        blank.append(b)
        if b["type"] == "text" and not any(x.get("_blank") for x in blank):
            blank.append({"type": "text", "text": "\n\n", "_blank": True})
    blank = [{k: v for k, v in b.items() if k != "_blank"} for b in blank]
    s, d = call(msgs + [{"role": "assistant", "content": blank}, user2], "replay_blank_text")
    report("replay_blank_text", s, d)

    # d) an empty text block.
    empty = [{"type": "text", "text": ""} if i == 0 else b for i, b in enumerate([None] + content)]
    s, d = call(msgs + [{"role": "assistant", "content": empty}, user2], "replay_empty_text")
    report("replay_empty_text", s, d)


main()

"""SMA-854 live probe. Reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the environment.

Prints block types, HTTP status, and input_transformations only. Never prints
the key or a signature. Raw responses go to OUT_DIR for fixture transcription.
"""
import json
import os
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

KEY = os.environ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"]
MODEL = os.environ.get("PROBE_MODEL", "claude-sonnet-5-5")
OUT_DIR = sys.argv[1]
ATTEMPTS = int(os.environ.get("PROBE_ATTEMPTS", "6"))

TOOLS = [
    {
        "name": "lookup_city_code",
        "description": "Return the internal code for a city. You need the code before you can get the weather.",
        "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]},
    },
    {
        "name": "weather_by_code",
        "description": "Get the weather for an internal city code.",
        "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"code": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["code"]},
    },
]

PROMPTS = [
    "Before you do anything, write one short sentence to me that says your plan. Then think carefully "
    "about which city codes might exist. Then write a second short sentence to me. Then call "
    "lookup_city_code for Paris.",
    "Answer in two separate parts with thinking in between: first tell me in one sentence what 17*23 is, "
    "then think again about whether Paris or Lyon is larger, then tell me that in one sentence, then call "
    "lookup_city_code for the larger city.",
    "Write a one-line greeting. Then reason step by step about the weather tool chain. Then write a "
    "one-line summary of your reasoning. Then call lookup_city_code for Paris.",
]


def call(messages, label):
    body = {
        "model": MODEL,
        "max_tokens": 8000,
        "thinking": {"type": "adaptive", "block_binding": {"prefix_mismatch_behavior": "drop_block"}},
        "output_config": {"effort": "max"},
        "tools": TOOLS,
        "messages": messages,
    }
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        "https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages",
        data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
        headers={
            "x-api-key": KEY,
            "anthropic-version": "2023-06-01",
            "anthropic-beta": "thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01",
            "content-type": "application/json",
        },
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=300) as r:
            status, data = r.status, json.loads(r.read())
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        status, data = e.code, json.loads(e.read() or b"{}")
    with open(os.path.join(OUT_DIR, f"{label}.json"), "w") as f:
        json.dump({"request_messages": messages, "status": status, "response": data}, f, indent=1)
    return status, data


def shape(content):
    out = []
    for b in content:
        t = b.get("type")
        if t == "text":
            out.append(f"text({len(b['text'].encode())}B)")
        elif t == "thinking":
            out.append(f"thinking({len(b.get('thinking', ''))}ch)")
        else:
            out.append(t)
    return out


def interleaved(content):
    """True when a thinking block follows a text block."""
    seen_text = False
    for b in content:
        if b["type"] == "text":
            seen_text = True
        elif b["type"] in ("thinking", "redacted_thinking") and seen_text:
            return True
    return False


def report(label, status, data):
    if status != 200:
        print(f"{label}: HTTP {status} {data.get('error', {}).get('message', '')[:300]}")
        return
    print(f"{label}: 200 stop={data.get('stop_reason')} shape={shape(data['content'])} "
          f"input_transformations={json.dumps(data.get('input_transformations'))}")


def main():
    found = None
    n = 0
    for attempt in range(ATTEMPTS):
        for pi, prompt in enumerate(PROMPTS):
            n += 1
            label = f"elicit_{attempt}_{pi}"
            msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]
            status, data = call(msgs, label)
            report(label, status, data)
            if status == 200 and interleaved(data["content"]) and data.get("stop_reason") == "tool_use":
                found = (msgs, data)
                break
        if found:
            break
    if not found:
        print(f"no interleaved shape in {n} attempts")
        return
    msgs, data = found
    content = data["content"]
    tool_results = [
        {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": b["id"], "content": "PAR-7351"}
        for b in content if b["type"] == "tool_use"
    ]
    user2 = {"role": "user", "content": tool_results}

    # a) exact replay: the split replay of the fix.
    s, d = call(msgs + [{"role": "assistant", "content": content}, user2], "replay_exact")
    report("replay_exact", s, d)

    # b) joined replay: what today's translator sends. All text joined at the
    # first text position.
    texts = "".join(b["text"] for b in content if b["type"] == "text")
    joined, placed = [], False
    for b in content:
        if b["type"] == "text":
            if not placed:
                joined.append({"type": "text", "text": texts})
                placed = True
        else:
            joined.append(b)
    s, d = call(msgs + [{"role": "assistant", "content": joined}, user2], "replay_joined")
    report("replay_joined", s, d)

    # c) a whitespace-only text block in the assistant message, after the first text.
    blank = []
    for b in content:
        blank.append(b)
        if b["type"] == "text" and not any(x.get("_blank") for x in blank):
            blank.append({"type": "text", "text": "\n\n", "_blank": True})
    blank = [{k: v for k, v in b.items() if k != "_blank"} for b in blank]
    s, d = call(msgs + [{"role": "assistant", "content": blank}, user2], "replay_blank_text")
    report("replay_blank_text", s, d)

    # d) an empty text block.
    empty = [{"type": "text", "text": ""} if i == 0 else b for i, b in enumerate([None] + content)]
    s, d = call(msgs + [{"role": "assistant", "content": empty}, user2], "replay_empty_text")
    report("replay_empty_text", s, d)


main()

**Why the probe did not run:** you are right that a key exists. It is in the repo `.env`, not in my shell. The permission system blocked two attempts to use it. First it blocked a grep of `.env`. Then it blocked a command that loaded `.env` into the probe process only. It classified both as access to credentials. I did not try another way around that block.

**How you can run it:** type this line in the prompt. The `!` prefix runs it in this session, so I see the output.

```
! cd /Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon && set -a && . ./.env && set +a && python3 -I /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-smaschek-dev-paigasus-paigasus-helikon/ca6d8245-7ac3-4613-8736-59ed8f192e5c/scratchpad/probe/probe.py /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-smaschek-dev-paigasus-paigasus-helikon/ca6d8245-7ac3-4613-8736-59ed8f192e5c/scratchpad/probe/out
```

The script uses only the Python standard library. It is at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-smaschek-dev-paigasus-paigasus-helikon/ca6d8245-7ac3-4613-8736-59ed8f192e5c/scratchpad/probe/probe.py`, and it does two things:

1. It asks `claude-sonnet-5-5` (adaptive thinking, effort `max`, `drop_block`) for a response where a thinking block follows a text block. It makes at most 18 calls.
2. If it gets that response, it sends the next request in four forms: the exact blocks (the fix), the joined text (what the code sends today), an added whitespace-only text block, and an added empty text block.

For each call it prints the block types, the status and `input_transformations`. It never prints the key or a signature. The `out/` folder then holds the raw responses, so I can transcribe test fixtures from a real trace. If you want me to run these probes myself in the future, you can add a permission rule for this kind of Bash command.

**Changes to the spec (no follow-up tickets):**

- **Core doc fix:** this PR now includes it, in a separate `docs(core)` commit. The commit gives the core a patch bump, and the dependent crates get a patch bump too.
- **Citations:** this was not a real limit. The API adds citations only for `document` or `search_result` blocks, or for server tools. The provider sends none of these, so a cited text block cannot occur. The spec now says this as a fact.
- **Blank text piece:** the probe tests if the API accepts a whitespace-only text block in an assistant message. If it does, the fix sends the blank piece, and the limit goes away. If it does not, the limit comes from the API, and the spec will cite the probe as evidence.
- **Live test:** after the probe, I will add an env-gated live test to `live_round_trip.rs` for this shape, with the prompt that the probe finds works.

GATE 1 is still open. When the probe results arrive, I fold them into the spec and ask you again for approval.
